Modern.tagline: A meditation studio. Sit. Notice. Leave.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Sati is the Pali word usually translated as 'mindfulness' — the core faculty trained in Vipassana and the Satipatthana Sutta. Strongest of Agent A's modern row: Anapana is narrower (just breath-awareness), Vihara reads as a building name. Sati is the practice itself in two syllables and lands cleanly on a modern wordmark without the Sanskrit-marketing baggage.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern meditation studios in 2025+ sit between the app-fatigued (Calm, Headspace, Insight Timer) and the retreat-curious. The opening is a small in-person studio that runs short, regular sits without scripts, soundtracks, or the wellness-industrial vocabulary. Patrons are 28-45, app-tired, and want a room and a teacher rather than a subscription.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Headspace (headspace.com) and Calm (calm.com) hold the app tier. Insight Timer (insighttimer.com) goes deeper for practitioners. MNDFL (mndflmeditation.com) is the closest in-person peer in NYC. We sit smaller, quieter, and Vipassana-grounded.
Modern.positioningStatement: A small Vipassana-leaning studio. Sit. Notice. Leave.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 45. Has done a Calm subscription and let it lapse. Has thought about a ten-day retreat but can't take the time off. Wants a room, a teacher, and forty-five minutes after work.
behaviors: Books a single sit, not a package
Walks from work; pays at the door
Sits twice a week and tells nobody

dos: Name the practice (anapana, body scan) without translating it
Publish the schedule and the teacher
Keep the website to one page
donts: Photograph people sitting on a beach

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — SATI CO. set in a low-contrast grotesk, wide kerned. A single dot above the I as the only mark. The dot alone works as the favicon and the door plaque.

colorPalette.name: Hall White
colorPalette.meaning: The colour of an empty meditation hall in morning light.

typography.primary: Söhne for the wordmark and schedule
typography.rationale: One family. The grotesk holds the studio register; the mono handles the printed schedule on the door.

Luxury.tagline: A small meditation hall in the Insight tradition.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Barre, Massachusetts is the home of the Insight Meditation Society (founded 1976 by Joseph Goldstein, Sharon Salzberg, Jack Kornfield) — the address that established serious Vipassana practice in the West. Strongest of Agent A's place row: Igatpuri is the Goenka HQ and risks reading as a knock-off, Rangoon is geopolitically charged. Barre is the quiet American address that the actual practitioners know.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury meditation is not spa-luxury — it is the small private hall with a senior teacher and a six-month waiting list. The opening is a members' sitting room positioned on lineage and silence rather than amenities. Patrons are 45+, often have a teacher already, and want a room in the city that respects that.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Insight Meditation Society (dharma.org) is the spiritual peer in Barre. Spirit Rock (spiritrock.org) holds the West Coast equivalent. Tergar (tergar.org) is the modern Tibetan-leaning peer. We sit as the urban members' hall for practitioners who already sit at IMS.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A members' sitting hall in the Insight tradition, in the city.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 70. Sits daily. Has done at least one IMS or Spirit Rock retreat. Wants a room with a senior teacher within walking distance of the office. Pays the annual fee without comment.
behaviors: Refers other members by quiet introduction
Holds the same cushion in the cupboard for years

dos: Refer to teachers by full name and lineage
Keep the door locked outside of sittings

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark. BARRE SIT in a quiet text serif, with a small brass disc beneath — the disc embossed on the member card and the door plate. No icon used digitally; the disc is a physical mark only.

colorPalette.name: Hall Cream
colorPalette.meaning: Beeswax candle, paper, the hall wall.

typography.primary: Lyon Text for the wordmark and printed material
typography.rationale: A classical text serif carries the lineage register; the grotesk handles the single digital surface.

Minimal.tagline: A meditation studio. Forty-five minutes at a time.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: The ten-day silent Vipassana course (as taught in the Goenka tradition since 1969) is the canonical entry to serious practice. Strongest of Agent A's evocative row: Noble Silence is the vow but reads severe, The Witnessing Seat is too descriptive. Ten Day Quiet borrows the retreat's gravity for a studio that runs short sits — the name carries weight without claiming to deliver the retreat itself.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal meditation is a room, a teacher, a bell, a clock. The opening is for a studio that publishes only the schedule and the teacher's name. Patrons want what they paid for — a quiet sit — and nothing else.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Insight Timer (insighttimer.com) holds the minimal-app tier. Othership (othership.us) does in-person well but with sauna theatre. MNDFL (mndflmeditation.com) is the closest minimal in-person peer. We publish less than any of them.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A meditation studio. Schedule, teacher, room. That's the website.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Sits already. Doesn't want a guided audio. Walks in, sits, walks out. Pays the monthly fee and reads no marketing email.

dos: Show only schedule and teacher on the homepage
Ring a bell at the start and end
Refund silently if the sit cancels

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. TEN DAY QUIET in a single grotesk weight, three lines stacked. No icon. The wordmark works on the door, the bench, and the schedule card. That is the entire system.

typography.rationale: One face. The door, the card, and the site all carry the same wordmark.

Corporate.tagline: Workplace meditation programs in the Burmese Vipassana tradition.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Sayadaw is the Burmese honorific for a senior monk-teacher (Mahasi Sayadaw, U Ba Khin, Pa Auk Sayadaw) — the lineage that gave Western Vipassana its method. Strongest of Agent A's heritage row for corporate: Goenka & Hall risks the Goenka organisation TM, Mahasi Method Studio reads single-studio. Sayadaw Group lands as a serious B2B partnership rooted in actual lineage rather than the secularised mindfulness vocabulary procurement is tired of.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate meditation in 2025+ has burned through the first wave — Headspace for Work, Calm Business, Modern Health. HR buyers want something quieter, in-person, and lineage-grounded rather than another app seat. The opening is a partnership-model group that places senior teachers inside large employers.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Headspace for Work (headspace.com/work) holds the app-B2B tier. Calm Business (business.calm.com) competes on subscription seats. Modern Health (joinmodernhealth.com) sits in the middle. We sit smaller, in-person, lineage-grounded.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Workplace meditation programs run by senior teachers, in the Burmese Vipassana tradition.

targetAudience.primary: HR directors and chief people officers at law firms, banks, and large tech employers. They've cancelled the Calm Business contract. They want a room in the office and a real teacher, on contract.
behaviors: Reviews teacher CVs as part of procurement

dos: Name each teacher with full lineage

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark — a single stacked square (the cushion seen from above) — to the left. Reads cleanly on uniforms, signage, and procurement decks.

typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed quarterly letters
typography.rationale: Inter scales cleanly across procurement decks; the serif handles the printed teacher letters.

Creative.tagline: A meditation studio built around the cushion.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The zafu is the round buckwheat-filled cushion that has been the seat of Zen meditation for centuries. Strongest of Agent A's craft row for creative: Cushion & Mat is fine but generic, Kapok Sit is too obscure for the audience. The Zafu Room reads as a designed studio that takes the object — the cushion — as its whole identity, like a printer's-shop or a tea room.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative meditation studios sit in the same register as a good independent tea room or stationery shop. Patrons are design-literate, often work in adjacent creative fields, and want a room that feels considered down to the cushion. The opening is a studio with a print-shop, illustrated, slightly bookish identity that doesn't drift into wellness-clip-art.
Creative.competitorLandscape: MNDFL (mndflmeditation.com) is the closest design-led peer. The Den Meditation (thedenmeditation.com) competes on aesthetics. Inscape (inscape.life) shaped the design template before closing. We sit warmer, more craft-led, and lineage-grounded.
Creative.positioningStatement: A meditation studio organised around the cushion.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 42. Designers, editors, architects. Buys good pencils and good notebooks. Will pay extra for a cushion that's been considered. Photographs the room — once — and never again.
behaviors: Asks which zafu fill the studio uses
Buys the studio's cushion for home

dos: Commission a yearly illustrated cushion chart
Print the schedule on heavy paper
Name each room after a fill (kapok, buckwheat, kombu)
donts: Use stock photos of women on cliffs

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a chunky display serif with letterpress-impression. The O of ZAFU is set as a small woodblock-style cushion seen from above. A standalone cushion mark for stickers and the bag tag.

typography.primary: GT Sectra Display for the wordmark and illustrated charts
typography.secondary: GT Sectra Book for the schedule and post-sit notes
typography.rationale: One family, two cuts. The display reads woodblock; the book weight handles the printed schedule.
